oneLiner: The largest US-listed AI rack integrator after Dell, now shipping at a ~$80B annual run-rate on NVIDIA Blackwell and Vera Rubin systems. The market is betting the earnings never turn into cash: it values Supermicro as if the revenue surge is a one-customer build-out funded by its own balance sheet.

verdict.stance: Positive - sized small for cash and governance risk
verdict.summary: The FY2027 question is no longer demand: Q1 ran ~30% above the top of guidance and the year was raised to $72-82B. The stock is priced as if FY2028 earnings fall sharply, so even a flat-margin, slow-growth year at a mid-single-digit multiple beats today's price, while the bear case needs a customer air pocket plus margin reversion to lose roughly half. What keeps the position small is cash: trailing operating cash flow is deeply negative against record profit, net debt is rising and the share count grows double digits a year. Two things would change the view: a second straight quarter of operating cash burn in Q2 FY27 alongside a new equity or convert raise, or any restatement or delay from the board's export-control review.
wtb: FY2027 revenue lands inside the $72-82B guide, which needs H2 revenue of roughly $32-42B after ~$40B in H1 - i.e. no air pocket when the largest customer's build-out ends.
GAAP gross margin holds at or above ~11% through FY2028 at this scale; each point is roughly $0.8B of pre-tax profit on $85B of revenue.
Cumulative operating cash flow for FY2027 turns positive by the Q4 FY27 report (Aug 2027) as $15B of inventory ships and customer prepayments grow.
Diluted shares stay below ~780M through FY2028 (Q2 FY27 guide assumes 753M GAAP), so EPS growth is not handed to converts and equity raises.

bear.why: The largest customer's build-out ends and Rubin orders go to Dell, HPE and ODMs; revenue falls ~29% from a ~$77B FY2027. Gross margin slips to ~9% as Supermicro chases volume, net margin ~4%, and another raise lifts diluted shares to ~780M. A shrinking integrator with negative cash flow gets a distressed multiple.

base.why: Rubin keeps revenue growing ~10% on FY2027 with concentration still high; gross margin ~10.5-11%, net margin ~5.5% on ~770M diluted shares. Cash conversion improves but stays erratic, so the market pays only a modest premium to today's discount, well below Dell.

bull.why: Rubin rack-scale DLC share gains plus the Cisco enterprise channel lift revenue ~43%; gross margin ~11.5-12% and net margin ~6.5% on ~770M shares. Positive operating cash flow and a clean ITGC opinion let the stock re-rate toward the lower end of hardware peers.

scenarioModel.note: EPS = revenue x net margin / diluted shares: bear $55B x 4.0% / 780M = $2.82; base $85B x 5.5% / 770M = $6.07; bull $110B x 6.5% / 770M = $9.29. FY2027 base of ~$77B = guide midpoint (Q1 $19.9B + Q2 guide $19.5-21.5B + implied H2). Net margin anchor: Q2 FY27 guide implies ~6.3% (GAAP EPS $1.59-1.83 x 753M shares on $19.5-21.5B). Multiples apply to FY2028 EPS at end-2027. Probability-weighted value ~$41.8 per share. Scenario inputs are Siberforge estimates, not consensus.

debates.q: Can the earnings become cash before the balance sheet runs out?
debates.bull: The burn is growth working capital, not losses: inventory and receivables built ahead of a $72-82B year, and current deferred revenue (customer prepayments) reached $4.3B at Sep 30, 2026. Q4 FY26 showed positive operating cash flow when shipments caught up.
debates.bear: Trailing operating cash flow is -$6.3B against $3.7B of net income (TTM through Sep 2026), net debt is ~$1.7B and rising, and the gap has been funded by converts and equity - diluted shares are up 13% YoY. EPS that has to be refinanced is worth a low multiple.
debates.view: This sets the multiple (6x vs 9x) more than revenue does. We need H1 FY27 operating cash flow near break-even; a second large burn plus a raise would move the stance to Neutral.

signpost.metric: Q2 FY27 operating cash flow and any new convert or equity issuance
signpost.threshold: bullish if Q2 OCF is positive; bearish if H1 OCF is below -$2B or a raise above $2B is announced

debates.q: Is ~12% the new gross-margin floor, or a stop on the way back to 9%?
debates.bull: Q1 FY27 GAAP gross margin of 12.7% came at four times last year's volume and above the 10.4-10.8% guide; rack-scale DLC and software/services carry more value than boxes. Company guidance points to ~12% for Q2 and FY2027 (unverified, secondary source).
debates.bear: The 17.5% in Q4 FY26 already halved toward 12.7% in one quarter on mix; management's own release warns margins may be lower as it targets larger customers, and Dell, HPE and ODMs price the biggest deals.
debates.view: Base case assumes 10.5-11% in FY2028, below today's run-rate, so the stock does not need the margin to hold - it needs it not to fall below ~9%.

signpost.threshold: 12% or higher confirms the floor; below 11% puts the bear case in play

debates.q: How much of FY2027 is one customer, and what follows it?
debates.bull: Nine customers exceeded $1B in FY2026, Cisco opened an enterprise channel in October 2026, and capacity is being built to 8,000+ racks a month by December 2026 for the Rubin cycle.
debates.bear: One data-center customer was 44% of Q1 FY27 revenue (vs 28% in FY2026) and two customers held 49% and 17% of receivables (call commentary, unverified); about $2.3B of Q1 revenue was delayed deployments catching up (unverified).
debates.view: The raised guide already implies H2 roughly flat to below H1, so a plateau is priced; a guide cut is not. Concentration is the single biggest swing factor between the bear and base cases.

signpost.metric: Q2 FY27 revenue vs $19.5-21.5B guide; FY2027 guide range; largest-customer share in the 10-Q
signpost.threshold: bearish if Q2 revenue is below $19.5B or the FY2027 guide is cut below $72B
signpost.when: Q1 FY27 10-Q (~Nov 2026) and Q2 FY27 report (~early Feb 2027)

thesis: Scale arrived faster than anyone modelled. Q1 FY27 revenue beat the top of the guide by ~$4.4B and the FY2027 range moved up by $7-10B; Supermicro is now a $70B+ revenue business one year after a $22B year.

The margin floor moved up. Operating margin went from ~4% a year ago to over 10% in Q1 FY27 at roughly four times the volume - operating leverage on a thin opex base, not just a one-quarter mix spike.

Rubin-cycle capacity is in place. Liquid-cooled rack-scale systems (DLC-2) are the bottleneck at Vera Rubin power densities, and Supermicro targets 8,000+ racks a month by December 2026, about half direct liquid-cooled.

The price assumes a collapse. The reverse DCF needs forward earnings to shrink ~10% a year for eight years after revenue compounded ~76% a year for three; even the bear case is not far below today's price.

latestQuarter.label: Q1 FY2027 (ended Sep 30, 2026; reported Nov 3, 2026; preliminary - closing not complete)
points: Net sales $19.9B vs $5.0B in Q1 FY26 and $11.1B in Q4 FY26; guide was $14.5-15.5B, Oct 20 preliminary $18.5-19.5B.
GAAP gross margin 12.7% (non-GAAP 12.8%) vs 17.5% in Q4 FY26 and a 10.4-10.8% guide; operating income $2.06B (10.4% margin).
GAAP net income $1.59B, diluted EPS $1.75 on 749M shares; non-GAAP EPS $1.81.
Operating cash flow -$0.43B; inventory $15.1B (+$2.2B q/q), receivables $9.7B (+$3.6B q/q); cash $6.9B vs bank debt and converts $8.6B.
Guide: Q2 FY27 net sales $19.5-21.5B, GAAP EPS $1.59-1.83 on 753M shares; FY2027 net sales raised to $72-82B from $65-72B.

latestProse: Q1 FY2027 (ended Sep 30, 2026; reported Nov 3, after an Oct 20 preliminary update). Net sales of $19.9B were roughly four times the year-ago quarter and well above both the original guide and the preliminary range; consensus was ~$15.8-16.4B depending on source. GAAP gross margin settled at 12.7%, down from Q4 FY26's mix-driven 17.5% but far above the 9-10% of FY2025, and GAAP diluted EPS was $1.75. The weak line was cash: operating cash flow was negative despite $1.6B of profit, as receivables and inventory absorbed it. The figures are preliminary: the release says closing procedures were not complete and the auditor had performed no procedures.
guidanceProse: Q2 FY2027 (Dec quarter) guide: net sales $19.5-21.5B, GAAP diluted EPS $1.59-1.83 and non-GAAP $1.66-1.90, on 753M GAAP / 769M non-GAAP diluted shares and a ~21% tax rate. FY2027 net sales were raised to $72-82B; with H1 near $40B, that implies H2 of roughly $32-42B, so the midpoint assumes no further sequential growth. Gross margin guidance of 12-12.5% for Q2 and 11.8-12.2% for the year was reported by a call summary but is not in the release (unverified). Management said the outlook does not assume the Q1 catch-up repeats (unverified). The release adds that margins may be lower and sales less predictable as Supermicro targets larger customers.
segments: Server and storage systems are the overwhelming majority of revenue; subsystems and accessories the small remainder.
AI/GPU rack-scale platforms are the growth engine; the CFO said more than 80% of revenue should be AI-related going forward (Q4 FY26 call).
Customers: hyperscale and neocloud data centers dominate (concentration in debate 3), with enterprise, sovereign and Cisco-channel demand the smaller, higher-margin tail.
competitive: Dell (ISG) and HPE bundle AI servers with services and financing and set pricing on enterprise and sovereign deals; Dell trades at a multiple well above Supermicro's.
Cisco is a channel, not a rival: its Secure AI Factory with NVIDIA integrates Supermicro liquid-cooled racks from October 2026.
ODMs (Quanta, Wiwynn, Foxconn) serve hyperscalers directly at thin margins and cap pricing on the biggest deals.
NVIDIA allocation is the gatekeeper: Supermicro ships GB300 NVL72 and HGX B300 at volume and markets Vera Rubin NVL72 and Rubin HGX systems.
Differentiators: time-to-market on each NVIDIA generation, building-block architecture, DLC-2 cooling scale and US manufacturing.
moat: Little structural moat in assembling GPU servers; Dell, HPE and ODMs can replicate most of the portfolio, which is why gross margin sat near 10% for years. Supermicro's edge is speed - first-to-market on each NVIDIA generation - plus rack-scale liquid-cooling integration and capacity at volume. That is a lead measured in quarters, renewed every platform cycle.
risks: Earnings are not cash. Trailing operating cash flow was -$6.3B against $3.7B of net income (TTM through Sep 2026, about -173%; -305% through June) as inventory and receivables grew with revenue; until that reverses, reported EPS overstates what shareholders can keep.

Balance sheet and dilution. Net debt was ~$1.7B at Sep 30, 2026 ($8.6B of bank debt and converts vs $6.9B cash), and diluted shares rose 13% YoY in Q1 FY27 (+11% in FY2026); further burn means more converts or equity, diluting the EPS the scenarios rely on.
Customer concentration. With one customer near half of Q1 revenue and receivables (debate 3), a single pause, delay or payment dispute shows up in one quarter, in both revenue and cash.

Governance is improving but not closed. The FY2026 10-K remediated three material weaknesses but one IT general controls weakness remained open at June 30, 2026; the board is reviewing certain export-control-related transactions that the company says could affect prior-period results, and employees face export-control indictments in the US and Taiwan (company not charged). Q1 figures were released before closing was complete.

Margin mean reversion. Gross margin fell from 17.5% to 12.7% in one quarter on mix, and the company warns larger customers mean lower margins; a return to ~9% would cut EPS by roughly a third at the same revenue.
catalysts: ~Nov 9-10, 2026: Q1 FY27 10-Q - confirms the preliminary figures, customer and receivables concentration, ITGC status (debates 1 and 3).
~Nov 18, 2026: NVIDIA Q3 FY27 report - Rubin ramp and supply as the read-through for rack demand (debate 3).
Dec 2026: 8,000+ racks per month capacity target, ~4,000 direct liquid-cooled.
~Early Feb 2027: Q2 FY27 report - revenue vs $19.5-21.5B guide, gross margin vs ~12%, operating cash flow (debates 1, 2, 3).
No set timetable: conclusion of the board's export-control transaction review; any finding that touches prior periods would reopen the accounting discount.

valPresets.note: Basis is forward earnings: FCF whipsaws with working-capital swings in a pass-through hardware model. The 12% discount rate carries the cash-conversion and governance overhang; the reverse DCF shows how little growth is priced.
